title: SESaMo: Symmetry-Enforcing Stochastic Modulation for Normalizing Flows
claim: Mapping a symmetric distribution to a canonical fundamental domain, transforming it, then mapping back makes a flow exactly symmetry-equivariant.
layout: 4 panels, left-to-right, labeled arrows between 1-D density sketches
description: Four small 1-D density sketches run left to right, each with axes and a thick black curve, joined by three thin horizontal arrows labeled with math. The first panel shows a symmetric Gaussian bump q_0 over z. An arrow labeled C_{T,z} leads to a second panel, where the density is folded onto the positive half-line as a sharp one-sided peak q_{z_c} over z_c. An arrow labeled g_θ leads to a third panel, where a shifted bump q_{z̃_c} over z̃_c has been moved away from the origin. The last arrow, labeled C^{-1}_{T,z}, leads to a fourth panel with two mirrored bumps q_θ over x, a symmetric bimodal density. The figure is black and white with no color or icons. The eye starts at the left Gaussian and follows the arrows to the bimodal result.
caption: Visualization of the canonicalization approach making a flow-based model equivariant with respect to a Z2 symmetry.
abstract: Deep generative models have recently garnered significant attention across various fields, from physics to chemistry, where sampling from unnormalized Boltzmann-like distributions represents a fundamental challenge. In particular, autoregressive models and normalizing flows have become prominent due to their appealing ability to yield closed-form probability densities. Moreover, it is well-established that incorporating prior knowledge - such as symmetries - into deep neural networks can substantially improve training performances. In this context, recent advances have focused on developing symmetry-equivariant generative models, achieving remarkable results. Building upon these foundations, this paper introduces Symmetry-Enforcing Stochastic Modulation (SESaMo). Similar to equivariant normalizing flows, SESaMo enables the incorporation of inductive biases (e.g., symmetries) into normalizing flows through a novel technique called stochastic modulation. This approach enhances the flexibility of the generative model, allowing to effectively learn a variety of exact and broken symmetries. Our numerical experiments benchmark SESaMo in different scenarios, including an 8-Gaussian mixture model and physically relevant field theories, such as the $Ï^4$ theory and the Hubbard model.
